title: Disclosure Through Permitted Tools
summary: Work through Disclosure Through Permitted Tools.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Disclosure Through Permitted Tools**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Security, § Disclosure Through Permitted Tools
blocks.md: Because a network-enabled tool adapter transmits its request parameters before receiving any response, confidential test fixtures embedded in a `package_search` query leak beyond the repair boundary even if the remote lookup returns no match. Traditional access control models evaluate tool invocations by the operational actions they perform or the remote state they mutate, treating read and search calls as benign because they leave the remote service unchanged. Enforcing task confidentiality, however, requires tracing information flow through the tool request itself.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Lethal trifecta matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: An agent that combines access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and an external communication channel can be steered to exfiltrate, and removing any one leg breaks the attack path.

questions.q: The section **Disclosure Through Permitted Tools** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Human approval binds to a digest of the canonical, host-resolved action, is presented out of band with the agent's explanation labeled untrusted, and is re-verified with its preconditions immediately before dispatch.

Over a trajectory an attacker gains an adaptation oracle and conversational momentum, so every dispatch is re-evaluated against policy and an obfuscated retry after a block is still the blocked action.
An agent that combines access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and an external communication channel can be steered to exfiltrate, and removing any one leg breaks the attack path.

When an agent acts for a requester, effective permission is the intersection of requester rights, service principal, task grant, and issuer and receiver policy, with identities taken from the runtime's task record, never from prompt text.
